metadata.title: Spectral Analysis of Systematic Residuals in Casimir Force Measurements: Methodological Pitfalls of Grid Interpolation and the Lomb-Scargle Resolution
metadata.description: Precision measurements of the Casimir force between macroscopic bodies have historically exhibited residual deviations, commonly attributed to surface roughness, patch potentials, and finite-temperature corrections. In this work, we present a spectral metrology pipeline designed to search for anomalous periodic components within Casimir force residuals. Using synthetic force-distance profiles, we validate that Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) analysis with Hann windowing can reliably detect harmonic anomalies with amplitudes down to 0.5% of the local force. We then apply this protocol to precision historical Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) data from Decca et al. (2003). Crucially, we demonstrate that standard spline interpolation of non-uniformly sampled AFM separation distances forcibly onto a uniform linear grid induces severe, spurious spectral peaks (>3 sigma significance) in FFT spectra. We resolve this artifact by implementing the normalized Lomb-Scargle periodogram directly on the raw, un-interpolated coordinates. The Lomb-Scargle analysis yields a False Alarm Probability FAP ~ 1.0, definitively establishing that the apparent periodic peaks are interpolation artifacts and confirming that historical residuals are consistent with experimental Gaussian white noise (chi2/ndof = 2.62). Our findings establish strict metrological guidelines for future nanomechanical tests searching for novel short-range interactions.
